metadata.title: SPARC Azure RBAC and Managed Identity Component Definition

components.title: Azure Managed Identity and RBAC Role Assignments
components.description: User-assigned managed identity with scoped RBAC role assignments for Key Vault, Storage, and Monitoring access. No passwords or service principal secrets are used. Deployed via Terraform (Azure/VM/modules/rbac/). <!-- UPDATE: Insert managed identity principal ID, client ID, and role assignment scope details for your deployment. -->

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 control implementations for Azure Managed Identity and RBAC

implemented-requirements.description: Account Management: A user-assigned managed identity is created for the VM, providing an Azure AD identity without passwords or certificates. The identity lifecycle is managed entirely through Terraform — creation, role assignment, and deletion are tracked as infrastructure-as-code. The identity is scoped to the resource group and assigned only to the VM via the identity block (type = UserAssigned). No shared or generic accounts are used. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000023, CIS Azure 1.1.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resource: azurerm_user_assigned_identity.main. The identity is assigned to the VM in the vm module via identity_ids.

implemented-requirements.description: Access Enforcement: Three scoped RBAC role assignments enforce access control: (1) Key Vault Secrets User — scoped to the Key Vault resource, granting read-only access to secrets for retrieving database credentials and application configuration; (2) Storage Blob Data Contributor — scoped to the Storage Account, granting read/write/delete access to blob data for application file uploads; (3) Monitoring Metrics Publisher — scoped to the resource group, granting permission to publish custom metrics. Each role is assigned to the managed identity's principal_id. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000033.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resources: azurerm_role_assignment.key_vault_secrets (Key Vault Secrets User), azurerm_role_assignment.storage_blob (Storage Blob Data Contributor), azurerm_role_assignment.monitoring (Monitoring Metrics Publisher).

implemented-requirements.description: Least Privilege: Each role assignment follows least privilege principles. The Key Vault role is Secrets User (read-only), not Secrets Officer or Administrator. The Storage role is Blob Data Contributor scoped to a single storage account, not a subscription-level Storage Account Contributor. The Monitoring role is Metrics Publisher (write metrics only), not Monitoring Contributor. No passwords, service principal secrets, or connection strings are used — the managed identity authenticates via Azure AD tokens with automatic rotation. Reference: DISA SRG-APP-000062, CIS Azure 1.3.
implemented-requirements.remarks: Terraform resources: All three azurerm_role_assignment resources use specific scope parameters (var.key_vault_id, var.storage_account_id, var.resource_group_id) rather than subscription-level assignments.
